structured_output.text:
The sets in question are exactly the $B_3$ sets (Sidon sets of order 3), and the statement $f(N)\sim N^{1/3}$ is an OPEN problem (the $h=3$ case of the Erdős–Turán / Bose–Chowla problem). It is neither proved nor disproved; what is known is:

1. Lower bound $f(N)\ge(1-o(1))N^{1/3}$ (Bose–Chowla). For a prime power $q$ and a generator $\theta$ of $\mathbb{F}_{q^3}^*$, let $A=\{a\in\mathbb{Z}/(q^3-1):\theta^a-\theta\in\mathbb{F}_q\}$. Then $|A|=q$. If $a_1+a_2+a_3\equiv b_1+b_2+b_3$ with $\theta^{a_i}=\theta+\alpha_i$, $\theta^{b_i}=\theta+\beta_i$, then $\prod(\theta+\alpha_i)=\prod(\theta+\beta_i)$; the difference of these two monic cubics over $\mathbb{F}_q$ has degree $\le2$ and vanishes at $\theta$, which has degree 3 over $\mathbb{F}_q$, so the cubics coincide and by unique factorization $\{\alpha_i\}=\{\beta_i\}$ as multisets. Thus $A$ is $B_3$ mod $q^3-1$, hence its lift to $\{1,\dots,q^3-1\}$ is a $B_3$ set of integers of size $q$. Taking the largest prime $p$ with $p^3-1\le N$ and using the prime number theorem gives $f(N)\ge(1-o(1))N^{1/3}$.

2. Upper bounds. If $|A|=k$, the $\binom{k+2}{3}$ sums $a+b+c$ ($a\le b\le c$) are distinct integers in $[3,3N]$, so $k\le(18N)^{1/3}(1+o(1))$. The best known bounds are Cilleruelo's $f(N)\le(4N)^{1/3}(1+o(1))$ and Green's $f(N)\le(7N/2)^{1/3}(1+o(1))\approx1.519N^{1/3}$.

Conclusion: $1\le\liminf f(N)/N^{1/3}\le\limsup f(N)/N^{1/3}\le(7/2)^{1/3}$. Whether the limit exists and equals 1 is unknown; it is a conjecture (believed true, analogous to the proven $B_2$ case $f_2(N)\sim N^{1/2}$ of Erdős–Turán and Singer) with no known proof or counterexample. I have proved only the stated bounds; closing the gap between the constants $1$ and $(7/2)^{1/3}$ remains open.
